extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and assembling newspaper copy about wartime air raids and their effects, combining official communiqués, casualty statistics, eyewitness vignettes, and scene descriptions to inform and convey impact to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution / identify origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly attribute facts, statements and statistics to their source (e.g., 'By the Associated Press', 'The Ministry of Information communique', 'Exchange Telegraph correspondent', 'British Press Association').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit attribution for official communiqués, government statements, wire service copy and eyewitness accounts; label the agency or speaker so readers can judge authority and verify. The page repeatedly cites AP, Exchange Telegraph, Air Ministry and Ministry of Information communiques as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official communiqués and statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate and quote official communiqués (e.g., Ministry of Information, Air Ministry) to report government-confirmed facts such as damage, casualties, and official assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present official communiqués verbatim or summarized with attribution; use them to establish confirmed facts (e.g., 'In the course of this morning's raids bombs were dropped on Buckingham Palace… Their majesties… were unharmed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Eyewitness and reporter vignettes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include first-person accounts from reporters and witnesses to humanize and illustrate the experience of raids (e.g., reporters' descriptions of running for shelter, hearing bomb whines, seeing fires, being thrown to the ground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, concrete anecdotes to convey immediate human impact and atmosphere; identify speakers/roles (reporter, telegraph operator, photographer) so readers understand perspective and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casualty and damage statistics (with sourcing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numeric totals for casualties, injuries, and material losses and indicate their provenance (e.g., 'London has suffered 1,175 dead and approximately 4,270 injured', 'box score lists sea warfare losses').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts explicitly and attach source or qualifier (estimated, reported, communique); include tabulated or summary 'box score' style lists when available to give readers a quantitative sense of scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological narrative and alarm/timeline detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconstruct the sequence and timing of events (alarms, duration of raids, times of all-clear signals, subsequent alarms) to orient the reader in when things happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List times and duration of alarms and attacks where possible (e.g., 'alarm lasting four hours and nine minutes and ending at 1:55 p.m.', 'first alarm came at 7:37 A.M.'); use chronology to show escalation and pattern of attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and landmark specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Name precise locations and landmarks affected (Buckingham Palace, Whitehall, Downing Street, St. Paul's Cathedral, East End, Thames estuary, specific streets and squares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pin damage and events to well-known places to convey significance and help readers visualize which civic and historic sites were hit; mention neighborhood, landmark, and relation between sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory and descriptive detail for vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sensory language (sounds, sights, smells, physical sensations) to convey the scene: whine of bombs, flashes, smoke, explosions, rubble, water geysers from burst mains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise sensory phrases to increase immediacy (as in many eyewitness passages). Avoid embellishment that would mislead about facts; keep descriptive detail tied to reported observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization with broader conflict and prior events
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the local incident in the wider war context (previous mass raids, other cities attacked, sea-war 'box score' totals, references to enemy strategy and earlier delayed-action bombs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals, trends and comparisons (e.g., 'London has suffered X dead since Saturday') and note related operations across regions to help readers understand scale and strategic pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of hard facts and interpretive/commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate news reporting (factual accounts, communiqués, eyewitness quotes) from editorial commentary or foreign press opinion (e.g., Daily Mail's comment on 'Berlin barbarians').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including opinion pieces or quoted commentary, label them as such and avoid conflating them with confirmed facts; present opposing perspectives with attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest details and symbolic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight stories and symbols that affect morale and public sentiment (e.g., the King and Queen sheltering and later visiting bombed areas; injured palace plumbers; destruction of chapel where princesses were christened).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such elements to show civic impact and morale implications, but tie them back to facts and avoid sensationalizing; note why a site or person is significant to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technical/military detail where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Include operational details when they aid understanding (types of bombs: incendiary, time bombs, high explosive; aircraft behavior: gliding with engines cut off; anti-aircraft barrage effectiveness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report technical details observed or from official sources to explain effects and defenses, but avoid speculative technical analysis without attribution; explain unfamiliar terms briefly if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on public services, emergency response and aftermath
rubrics_metrics.description: Document responses by fire services, auxiliary units, police, volunteers (suicide squads dealing with time bombs), and note services disrupted (Thames excursion boat service, buses, elevators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe emergency actions and continuity or interruption of civic services to inform readers about safety and practical consequences; attribute statements about service status to officials.
